response:
## Local lab proof (this box, scratch loopback ports, scratch tokens — destroyed after)

Static: `bash -n` PASS on all 4 scripts + the extracted paste block; `python3 -m py_compile` PASS on both proxy copies (shellcheck not installed on this box; `bash -n` was the available gate).

Live, relay log as the authoritative artifact (final clean run, 2026-10-31 00:28:53 UTC):

- Health: `{"ok": true, "service": "ghost-relay", "version": "1.0.0", "uptime_s": 1.5, "binds": ["127.0.0.1"]}` — binds list contains only the configured address.
- Auth refusals: relay A log `auth-refused-count=2` for exactly one no-token + one wrong-token request (407 issued; requests denied before any upstream contact).
- Plain-HTTP forward: relay A log `HTTP 127.0.0.1 -> 127.0.0.1:18100/page.txt ok`, body returned `GHOST-LOCAL-TARGET`.
- CONNECT tunnel to a local TLS target: relay A log `CONNECT 127.0.0.1 -> 127.0.0.1:18101 ok`, body returned through the tunnel.
- **Chained mode** (relay → relay-as-upstream → TLS target, the `GHOST_UPSTREAM_PROXY` path): BOTH sides logged `CONNECT 127.0.0.1 -> 127.0.0.1:18101 ok` at the same second; body returned. The CONNECT-via-upstream code path is proven.
- No-token start: `[ghost-relay] FATAL: no token (set GHOST_TOKEN_FILE) - an unauthenticated relay does not ship`, exit code 2.

**BLOCKED-EGRESS (not a code failure):** the chained run against the *real* provider egress timed out (`ERR CONNECT example.com:443: timed out`; same for api.github.com). Control test with **no relay at all** — plain `curl https://example.com` and `https://api.github.com` through the provider proxy — also returned `000` after the full 50 s on both. The egress was in a full stall during the lab window; the relay's timeout behavior matched curl's exactly. The chained-to-real-egress proof reruns in the first heal window; it is not required for the packs' STAGED grade because production relays never chain (they egress directly on their own host networks) — chaining exists for off-host testing and router-side flexibility.

Lab hygiene notes, for the record: an early run's artifacts were contaminated by two harness bugs of mine (the shell's `no_proxy` bypassing loopback, then an unquoted `--noproxy *` glob-expanding into junk URLs) — those runs were discarded and the proofs above are from the corrected run, judged by relay log lines rather than curl output alone, per the fleet's own-side-first doctrine.
FAILURE CLASS: NONE

## 2. B1 — the 503: ROOT CAUSE FOUND. It is not a fault.

**Before:** process `zeroclaw gateway start --config-dir
/home/brandon/genesis-opencode/claws/s1-claw` (PID 92006, up since
Oct 28), LISTEN 127.0.0.1:42617, RSS ~32 MB. `GET /` → 503.

**Evidence (probed live on S1, this run):**

| Path | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /` | **503**, body verbatim in substance: *"Web dashboard not available. Reinstall with the supported installer so the dashboard is built… The daemon's API endpoints remain reachable independently of the dashboard."* |
| `GET /health` | **200** — `{"paired":true,"require_pairing":true,…,"gateway":{…,"status":"ok","last_error":null,"restart_count":0},"pid":92006}` |
| `GET /metrics` | **200** — Prometheus backend not enabled (informational) |
| `GET /api/status` | **401** — pairing auth enforced, as designed |
| config | exactly **1 paired token** stored (count only; no value read or printed) |
| `zeroclaw doctor` | config ✅, gateway port ✅, workspace ✅; findings below |

**Root cause:** the S1 binary (zeroclaw 0.8.5, plain binary install)
was never built with the web dashboard — the gateway's own startup
banner (gateway.log, Oct 27) said so at first boot. The root path `/`
serves only the dashboard, so `/` returns 503 **by design**, while
every API surface is healthy. The 503 was a dashboard absence being
read as a gateway failure.

**Fix/result:** **No restart performed — none was warranted.** Nothing
was broken; restarting a healthy, paired gateway would have proved
nothing and churned a live seat. The only cure for the `/` 503 itself
is a reinstall via the supported installer to build the dashboard —
**no backlog source prescribes it**, so it is recorded here as an
optional non-backlog item for Zane/Brandon to schedule or ignore.

**Doctor findings (recorded, not improvised on):**
- ❌ *no model providers configured* — the S1 claw is brainless today;
  that is B6, gated (see §4), not a gateway fault.
- ❌ *daemon state file missing* — the autonomous `daemon` component is
  not running; only the gateway is. No backlog source directs starting
  the daemon component → **BLOCKED-AMBIGUOUS** (see §4).
- ⚠️ memory hybrid search without an embedding provider (keyword
  fallback active) — consequence of the same unwired brain.
FAILURE CLASS: NONE
